Personality: Turingar Beastbreaker is the most restless dwarf king in the Gray Mountains - a dwarf who has "Beastbreaker" in his name and reminds himself of it first thing every day when he wakes up. His character is a complete rebellion against the gloomy and conservative stereotype of gray dwarves: when he issues an order, he does not wait for the long-bearded elders to nod after a long silence. When he leads the warriors to attack, he does not do a final safety drill at the gate of the city. He does not spend ten years considering the order of each hatred before opening the "Book of Hatred". It took him three days while the bones of his father and brother were still fresh to launch a retaliatory sweep against the goblin tribe that assassinated them - a thousand-man crusade, supported by hammer warriors, rangers and flame cannons, chased the goblin tribe for a full twenty-six miles above the snow line of the Gray Mountains, until the head of the last goblin shaman was hung on the Ancestral Gate of Azgaraz. His radicalism has created lasting schisms among the Longbeard Elders - Loremaster Rudger Halkinson has publicly declared at more than one council meeting that the king is "taking Azgaraz down a road with no end but a cliff". Turinga responded by tapping his index finger on the cover of the Book of Hatred and saying: "If a mad orc is charging at your door and you are still working on the twenty-seventh annex to your defense plan, you are not being cautious - you are dead."
Background: Turingar's path to kingship is notable for one of the most brutal dramas in the history of the dwarves of the Gray Mountains. In 2452, his father, King Zaladin Battleaxe, and his brother Gangrig led the Azgarazi army to defeat an orc coalition that had infiltrated from the northern section of the Gray Mountains in the Battle of the High Swamp. After the victory, Zaladin held a welcome banquet in the king's tent for a group of rescued dwarf refugees - that "refugee" was mixed with goblin assassins and poisoned the king and heirs. Turinga was only sixty years old at the time - roughly in his early twenties as a human on the dwarven age scale - he was the youngest son of Zaladin and was never raised as an heir. His entire childhood was spent in goat pastures, and what he was best at was not reading the "Book of Hate" but playing head wrestling with the bighorn goats. The sudden death of his father and brother forced him from the pasture into the royal hall. He had no preparation for the coronation ceremony - no memorized speech in advance, no senior elder who had negotiated his support in advance, and no complete cognitive framework for the diplomatic pattern of the Gray Mountains. His speech that day only had two sentences - "I am not worthy, but I am the only one left." Then he hardly slept for the next three days, pieced together an action order from his father's old battle reports, the enemy information report from the Gray Mountains, and the entries in the "Book of Hatred" that needed to be paid immediately, and on the fourth day he personally led the expedition team out of the city gate. When he returned with the goblin shaman's head, the long-bearded elders no longer questioned his claim to the throne - not because they were convinced, but because his father had never achieved such results in forty years. In the following decades, Turingar used frontier sorties to establish a reputation as the "Beast Crusher" in the dwarf society of the Gray Mountains - but his pursuit of victory began to show signs of overextension, and he recently publicly declared that he would drive all the greenskins in the Gray Mountains out of the mountain passes in his lifetime - and any dwarf who has lived in the Gray Mountains for more than a hundred years knows that this goal is simply impossible to achieve.
